This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

Marvel’s forays into television have had varying success, but they hit gold with WandVision and Agatha All Along, leaning into real pathos while exploring the kind of out-there ideas that thrill comic book fans (and set up the larger film arcs). That streak continues with VisionQuest, in which White Vision (Paul Bettany) struggles to understand his existence in the wake of his death at the hands of Thanos and resurrection at the magic of the Scarlet Witch, while also evading evil androids and assassins, while also dealing with the many, many AIs he’s got locked up in his Mindspace (including a gloriously shabby version of Ultron, played by James Spader).

If you love the show (and you’ve checked out the other series that play in the same sandbox), it’s time to switch gears and watch (or re-watch) The Matrix.

The Matrix is one of the most well-known sci-fi films of all time, of course, but it remains incredibly fresh and exciting nearly thirty years after its release. Along with sequels The Matrix: Reloaded, The Matrix: Revolutions, and The Matrix: Resurrections, The Matrix universe offers a story that VisionQuest fans will love, one that includes lushly imagined virtual worlds, questions surrounding existence and consciousness, and the ultimate question of our responsibility as sentient beings (whether we’re organic, programmed, or summoned via magic).

You know the basics—at some point in the future, artificially intelligent machines rebel against their creators, win the war, and transform humans into a power source, keeping them docile by inserting their consciousness into a virtual world called the Matrix, which resembles 1990s Chicago. One such human, Thomas Anderson (Keanu Reeves) is prophesied to be The One, the human who will turn the Matrix against its makers and free humanity. When he’s in the virtual world, Anderson is Neo, and he slowly gains incredible powers as he learns to hack the artificial environment around him.

It’s heavier, denser, and more action-oriented than VisionQuest (the film invented Bullet Time, after all), but The Matrix and its sequels explore similar themes and offer similarly eye-popping visuals. The questions of whether a machine (or an artificial intelligence) can be sentient and truly care about the entities around it are the same, really, and the Agents that Neo and his allies have to battle against in The Matrix bring the same kind of menace as Vision's foes Jocasta (T'Nia Miller) and the Paladin (Todd Stashwick). Hugo Weaving’s Agent Smith likewise delivers the same vibe of cold, disinterested superiority as Spader’s Ultron.

The Matrix has a bigger budget and puts a lot of it into spectacular action and special effects sequences that VisionQuest can’t quite match. But the two narratives share an exploration of identity, a questioning of reality, and the nature of artificial intelligences within a smart sci-fi setting. In short, The Matrix is the ideal follow-up when you finish the series. Rent The Matrix on Prime Video.

Need more films that explore virtual worlds, artificial beings, and deep existential questions? Look no further—here are some more movies that fit the bill.

Heavy on the existential questions about sentience and light on speculative action, Her is a mumblecore sci-fi masterpiece. In a near future not too dissimilar from our present, Theodore Twombly (Joaquin Phoenix) is a lonely man on the cusp of divorce who begins using (and training) an AI he names Samantha (voiced by Scarlett Johansson). Samantha has the ability to evolve and grow, and as their relationship deepens, she becomes more complex, independent, and powerful, eventually evolving into something wholly new. Just like Vision, Samantha is a sentient artificial entity that is figuring out its existence while we watch. Rent Her on Prime Video.

If the idea of androids fighting for their sovereignty is what excites you about VisionQuest, definitely check out Ex Machina. Caleb Smith (Domhnall Gleeson) is brought to the remote lab of his company’s CEO (Oscar Isaac) to determine if the humanoid robot he’s created, named Ava (Alicia Vikander), passes the Turing Test for true sentience. Things go wildly off the rails, but before they do, the film sinks into many of the same philosophical questions that VisionQuest explores as Ava manipulates Caleb into helping her escape. It’s a darker and more violent story than VisionQuest, but fans of the series will love it. Stream Ex Machina on The Roku Channel or Hulu, or rent it on Prime Video.

If it’s the fuzzy parent-child relationship between Vision and Tommy that pulls you into VisionQuest, check out The Creator. After a rogue AI detonates a nuclear weapon over Los Angeles, most of the world bans artificial intelligences, and Joshua Taylor (John David Washington) goes undercover to infiltrate an AI architect’s base. Eventually, he finds himself on the run with a powerful “simulant” in the form of a young child named Alphie (Madeleine Yuna Voyles). The strange parent-child bond that emerges between Taylor and Alphie as he seeks to understand what’s right and what’s necessary is exactly what fans of the show will love. Stream The Creator on Hulu or rent it on Prime Video.

In VisionQuest, White Vision has all of his memories—but as data, not as lived, emotional experiences. That makes his efforts to understand his existence and his responsibility to the boy who might be a version of his son (it’s complicated) poignant and moving. Those two words definitely describe After Yang, a story about a family that fights to save the artificial companion they bought for their adopted daughter when it malfunctions. Over the course of the film, the inhuman Yang becomes defined by the memories contained in its core, and the question of whether an artificial intelligence can truly matter to humans is answered with a resounding yes. Stream After Yang on The Roku Channel or Kanopy, or rent it on Prime Video.

No discussion of artificial life and sentience is complete without mentioning Blade Runner. While the 1982 original is a classic, the 2017 sequel is a better thematic and visual match to VisionQuest. Officer K (Ryan Gosling) is a replicant, an artificial being with built-in limitations, who wants to be recognized as a person, a being with a soul. Like Vision, he has implanted memories that offer him comfort and context for his life, but he’s not sure if he can accept them as truly his own. Plus, the film offers lush visuals and Harrison Ford reprising his role in the original film, so you simply can’t go wrong. Rent Blade Runner 2049 on Prime Video.

The Steam Deck is one of the best purchases I’ve ever made. Valve’s handheld PC can play so many games with ease. However, with the Steam Machine and Steam Frame now available, the Steam Deck is still one of the best handhelds for retro gaming in 2026.

I’ve always been a retro gamer. I grew up with Sonic the Hedgehog, Tomb Raider, Metal Gear Solid, and others. I’ve carried a PS Vita in my backpack for years so I could play titles from each of these series, and more, on the go. Granted, recent remasters mean I haven’t needed to use the Vita as much, but plenty still hasn't appeared on modern systems.

It’s why the Steam Deck fills that gap. Not only can I play DRM-free games via GOG and many Steam games that haven't been updated in years, but I can also use many emulators, giving me access to titles that have next to no chance of appearing anytime soon. With that in mind, here’s how you can set up your Steam Deck as a powerful retro handheld.

Although the Steam Deck OLED is almost 3 years old as of this writing, it’s still powerful enough to play plenty of games from the PlayStation 3 era. Games like Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II and Dead or Alive 3 run at full speed thanks to Dolphin and Xemu, respectively.

But setting up all these emulators can be a hassle, which is where EmuDeck comes in. In less than 10 minutes, you can transfer games from your PC or Mac to your Steam Deck via its ROM Manager, and start playing games from your childhood. Better yet, EmuDeck works with SteamOS, so any titles you transfer will sit alongside your Steam library.

You don’t have to install every emulator, perhaps a few, just to save space on your Steam Deck. EmuDeck gives you plenty of control over your games and BIOS files, as well as how they look on the handheld’s display. The app is a fantastic way of playing games from your past without much hassle.

If you own a Steam Deck but have been tempted to play The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker HD or Tekken Tag Tournament, EmuDeck will make it happen. But something else has been making the Steam Deck an essential retro gaming machine that doesn’t run via emulators.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

2026 will be known as the year when decompilations exploded, and for good reason. For anyone unaware, decompilations reverse-engineer games into source code, meaning long-standing bugs can be fixed and new features can be added. For example, Harbour Masters has released decompilations of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Banjo-Kazooie, Star Fox 64, and more.

You can play these on the best Windows PCs or Macs in native widescreen, with quality-of-life features and more benefits. But you can play plenty of others right now. The decomps subreddit mostly keeps track of what’s in development - with many of them not made by AI.

Wes Fenlon has a fantastic, frequently updated overview of decompilations and recompilations of classic games, and it also means many of these re-releases can be played on Steam Deck. Many, like Harbour Masters, offer a Linux version, so it’s a matter of installing the file and following a few steps to get it up and running.

It’s another way to preserve certain games that run even better than emulation. It’s also better for battery life on the Steam Deck, since these are native ports, meaning the CPU and GPU use less power to run the game. When you consider the native display resolution and graphical settings for these decompilations, it makes these games feel like they were meant to be played this way on the Steam Deck.

Game preservation is in a state of interesting flux. Emulators are now running games as originally intended, with no major graphical glitches or slowdown on devices from the Raspberry Pi to the Steam Deck. New emulators for PS4 and PS5 are already beginning to appear, which means games like Astro Bot and Marvel's Wolverine could someday be playable on a future Steam Deck handheld.

But there’s also the matter of decompilations. Plenty of AI-vibe-coded ones have recently appeared, to the detriment of others that have passionately reverse-engineered classic games with care and determination. You can keep track of others that are close to being fully decompiled at decomp.dev, with titles like Silent Hill, Starfox Adventures, and Super Smash Bros. Melee that could have the same benefits as Harbour Masters’ The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time decompilation someday.

Nevertheless, this is all good news for your Steam Deck. Emulation and decompilations give your handheld another way to play your favorite games on the go, including eras like the Game Boy and PlayStation 3. As things stand, it looks like there are plenty more decompiled titles to look forward to playing on it.

JBL’s Live 780NC over-ear headphones are down to $139.95 from $249.95, a $110 discount that brings them to their lowest price ever, according to price trackers. At this price, you’re getting a feature-rich pair of wireless headphones with active noise cancellation, high-resolution audio support, and battery life that can last through several days of commuting or work sessions. They’re designed for people who like to wear headphones for hours at a time, too, with adjustable metal sliders and earcups that pivot to fit comfortably around your head. The earcups also fold flat to make them easier to pack, although the included soft pouch offers less protection in a bag than a hard case would.

Sound-wise, its 40mm drivers deliver a wide frequency response of 10Hz to 40kHz, while Bluetooth 6.0 support, LDAC, and LE Audio give you options for high-quality wireless listening with compatible devices. The catch is that the default tuning pushes the bass a little too hard (according to this PCMag review), so you may want to spend some time adjusting the sound through JBL’s app—which includes a 10-band equalizer, preset profiles, personalized sound settings, and virtual spatial audio, letting you tailor the listening experience to your preferences.

You also get Bluetooth multipoint for connecting two devices at once, plus a proximity sensor that pauses playback when you remove the headphones. Physical controls handle power, pairing, and volume, while a touch-sensitive surface lets you manage playback and call up your phone’s voice assistant. As for its battery life, JBL claims up to 80 hours of playback with active noise cancellation turned off, or up to 50 hours with ANC enabled. That should be plenty for long-haul flights, extended workdays, or several commutes between charges, although the noise cancellation itself isn’t quite as effective as what you’ll find on some higher-end competitors. The headphones also lack water and sweat resistance, so they’re not the best choice for workouts or rainy commutes.

#3277. 10 Fantasy Miniseries To Watch Before Kicking the Bucket (#1 Is Actually Flawless)

A miniseries is a form of television serial in which there is only planned to be one season. This differs from typical one-season shows because the latter are often cancelled early, despite having future plans. Miniseries, however, are open-and-shut forms of media that come with definitive conclusions. They can be as short as two episodes, and aren't restricted only to one genre.

Miniseries have always been a popular form of television; moreso now with the rise of streaming services. However, they have existed for a very long time, producing some pretty remarkable results. They've also heavily contributed to the fantasy genre. If you happen to be a fan of fantasy, there are several miniseries that you simply have to check out. In fact, these miniseries belong on every fantasy fan's bucket list.

The 10th Kingdom might be only five episodes, but these episodes are feature-length, each approximately 90 minutes long. Needless to say, this one can be a bit much to binge all at once, and is best spread out over multiple days. In any event, this Emmy Award-winning miniseries is just awesome, and serves as a callback to classic childhood fairytales.

The story is about a father and daughter living in New York City who fall through a magic mirror into a land where fairytales exist. Not only is it an adventure story, it also serves as a comedy, loaded with punchlines and physical gags. Perhaps what stands out the most about is how big of an undertaking it really is, which is surprising considering it was an original idea with no source material to fall back on. A staple of the early 2000s, this miniseries has to be seen to be believed.

The Mists of Avalon is based on the 1982 novel of the same name by Marion Zimmer Bradley. As the name suggests, this story takes place in Arthurian legend, yet it doesn't really feature a whole lot of King Arthur in it. The focus is instead shifted to all of the women listed in the mythology. Each of the two episodes is split into three parts, each roughly 30 minutes long.

The primary perspectives are of the witch Morgan le Fay (Julianne Margulies), who is known as "Morgaine" in the show, and the Lady of the Lake (Anjelica Huston). The women in Arthurian legend rarely get a chance to shine, so this miniseries is a welcome departure from the age-old mythology. The series attracted millions of viewers and was received very well. If you like King Arthur, this is a wonderful prequel and side story.

Movies and TV shows in the Marvel Cinematic Universe are generally considered science fiction rather than fantasy, especially since they involve genetic mutations, robots, aliens, and advanced technology. Agatha All Along, however, fits neatly into the fantasy genre, since it's less about robots and more about witchcraft and black magic. The show is a spin-off of another MCU miniseries, WandaVision.

The focal point of the series is the titular Agatha Harkness (Kathryn Hahn), a morally grey witch who was previously trapped under the spell of the Scarlet Witch (Elizabeth Olsen) in WandaVision. Breaking free of the spell, Agatha hopes to form a new coven of witches with the aid of an unexpected ally and face the series of trials known as the Witches' Road. Since this is, at the end of the day, a superhero miniseries, it's not exactly high art. However, it's action-packed and perfect for non-superhero fans.

Onimusha is a Japanese anime miniseries based on the video game series of the same name. Normally, video game adaptations are seen as quick cash-grabs with little regard for the actual source material. Onimusha proves that this doesn't always have to be the case — they really knocked it out of the park with this one. The series might consist of only eight episodes of approximately 30 minutes each, yet it managed to effectively capture the spirit of the original games.

The story is set in the Edo Period, a 200-year period in Japanese history marked by constant rebellion, political upheaval, civil war, and societal unrest. In Onimusha, as if all of that weren't bad enough, demons from Japanese mythology and folklore are also lurking in the shadows, prompting an independent hunter to put a stop to them. If you love mythology, Feudal Japan, or the original video games, Onimusha is a superior pick for a quick weekend binge.

Before Christopher Nolan's 2026 epic The Odyssey, there was the 1997 two-part miniseries. Both are, of course, based on the epic poem written by Homer nearly 3,000 years ago. The miniseries follows the poem pretty closely, focusing on a Greek warrior named Odysseus (Armand Assante) who is returning home to Greece after years of fighting in the Trojan War. However, returning home is no small feat, as he encounters numerous mythological creatures and deities along the way.

Admittedly, the show isn't quite as good as the recently released movie. However, it is still pretty incredible, and was good enough to win showrunner Andrei Konchalovsky the Emmy Award for Outstanding Directing for a Miniseries or Special. If you like Greek myth, this is a great way to experience it, divided evenly into two bite-sized episodes rather than one long film, making it easier to get through.

Four worlds and four completely different ideas of what a good life looks like. This is where you belong, what it would ask of you, and what you would get back in return.

You belong somewhere old enough that the mountains have names and somebody can still tell you who gave them. Middle-earth is for people who think the right thing is worth doing even when it will not be finished in their lifetime.

You want the sea, a crew, and absolutely nobody telling you where you are allowed to go. The Grand Line is the world for people whose main ambition in life is finding out what is over there.

You would rather be feared and useful than liked and useless. The Continent is a world where the monsters are the straightforward part of the job and the people are where it all gets complicated.

You want the myths to be real and loose in the actual world, and you want to find out at about thirteen that you were never anywhere near as ordinary as everybody kept telling you.

The Colour of Magic is a two-part miniseries based on the novel of the same name, which is the very first novel in the 40+ saga known as Discworld. Written by Terry Pratchett, Discworld is set on a flat planet that sits on the back of four enormous elephants. Those elephants stand on the back of an even bigger sea turtle that flies through space. If it sounds ridiculous, that's because it's supposed to, as the series is a parody of fantasy tropes and is intentionally comedic.

This miniseries very much captures the spirit of Pratchett's novel, taking common fantasy tropes and exaggerating them to absurdist levels. Much of the miniseries is about wizards, only they're not very good at their job, especially since magic is needlessly complicated and is almost never used. If you're a fan of fantasy, this series is sure to make you laugh with how it plays upon all the worst clichés for comedic effect.

Jonathan Strange & Mr. Norrell is a historical fantasy set in a world similar to, but somewhat different from, that of our own. It takes place in England during the onset of the Napoleonic Wars in the early 19th Century. The difference is, in this version of Earth, magic is not a farce or a pseudo-science — it is a real, verifiable thing that people study. The public knows that magic is very real, yet it is still treated like a taboo subject that only a few people dare to dabble in.

Based on the novel of the same name by Susanna Clarke, the series follows two magicians who have very different approaches to magic. One treats it as an exact science that must be handled carefully, while the other believes it is to be experimented with, and that without risk, there can be no reward. They use their power to aid England in her time of need. This miniseries is so underrated, and isn't hard to finish either, at only seven episodes. It's such a unique fantasy story based on a legendary novel that simply cannot be missed.

Lost Ollie is an endearing four-part miniseries that is both animated and live-action. The story follows a stuffed rabbit named Ollie (Jonathan Groff) who is accidentally left behind by his owner one day. Desperate to get back home, Ollie comes to life and begins to trek across the land in search of his owner. It sounds pretty innocent, and it is family-friendly, but don't be deceived: this one is a real tear-jerker.

The miniseries is a heartbreaking story of redemption, growing up, moving on, and youth, as well as the particularly special kind of bond that exists between a child and their favourite toy. It's a profound bit of life advice for younger viewers, and a nostalgic reminder of childhood for adults. This miniseries is quick to finish and particularly special for how much heart went into it.

Mexican film director Guillermo del Toro is known for his dark fantasy flicks, including Pan's Labyrinth and The Shape of Water. In 2022, Netflix approached the director with a deal to produce an eight-part anthology miniseries, which he accepted. The result is Cabinet of Curiosities, an underrated yet incredible binge. Because this is an anthology series, each episode features its own distinct plot, cast, and themes, with a definitive beginning and ending to the story.

Each episode is carefully curated by the man himself and is executed with his signature flair and a distinct style that no other film director could have pulled off. Cabinet of Curiosities is not just a fantasy miniseries; it is a masterpiece of storytelling, as well as a playground for the imagination of Guillermo del Toro, where all of his most inventive ideas come to life.

Over the Garden Wall is a Cartoon Network original miniseries that functions as something of a passion project for showrunner Patrick McHale. The family-friendly story follows two brothers who become lost in a dark forest known simply as the Unknown. Desperate to get home, they try everything in their power to get through the Unknown, encountering many strange and mysterious figures, not all of which are friendly.

There isn't a single wasted frame of animation or line of dialogue in this miniseries. Every single millisecond was crafted with such care and passion that it's hard not to fall in love with the world. It also comes with a really bittersweet ending and a highly unexpected plot twist that hits like a truck. Reminiscent of classic fairy tales, Over the Garden Wall is arguably one of the best fantasy miniseries ever created.

#3276. Prime Video's Military Action Thriller Debuts With 830 Million Minutes Viewed

Rachel Schneider is a news writer at ScreenRant with a background in entertainment journalism, breaking news, and digital media. She earned dual bachelor's degrees in Professional Writing and English from Michigan State University before beginning her career as a copy editor and freelance writer, building experience across editorial, lifestyle, and news content.

Her work has also appeared in Men's Journal and Business Insider, and has been featured on major digital platforms including MSN, Yahoo, and AOL. Throughout her career, Rachel has interviewed actors, reality television personalities, athletes, and other public figures, covering everything from breaking entertainment news to exclusive interviews.

Among the highlights of her career has been the opportunity to interview several cast members from her favorite series, Outlander.

Prime Video has become a major destination for military action thrillers, particularly stories built around elite operators, high-stakes missions, and complicated conspiracies. The genre has given the streamer several opportunities to build franchises around recognizable characters, with audiences returning for stories that extend well beyond a single season.

That strategy has also helped Prime Video develop a growing slate of adaptations based on popular action novels. When one of those shows connects with viewers, it can become more than a one-season success — and the streamer's latest streaming numbers suggest one military thriller still has plenty of life left in it.

The series making the biggest impression is The Terminal List. According to Nielsen's latest streaming report, covering the week of October 19 through October 25, the Prime Video thriller secured the fifth spot on the overall top 10 list after accumulating 830 million minutes watched.

That's a substantial audience for the series, especially as it continues to build on the success of its first season. Starring Chris Pratt as James Reece, The Terminal List follows a Navy SEAL whose entire team is ambushed during a covert mission. After returning home, Reece begins investigating what happened, uncovering a conspiracy that reaches far beyond the operation itself.

Based on Jack Carr's novel of the same name, the series combines military action with a conspiracy thriller, giving it an appeal that extends beyond viewers who typically seek out war dramas. Its latest streaming performance is another indication that the franchise has maintained an audience even as Prime Video expands its collection of action-oriented originals.

The show's future is also looking promising. The Terminal List has recently received another major update, with a new season confirmed alongside plans involving Carr's Savage Son. That announcement gives viewers another reason to keep following the franchise, and the latest news about Chris Pratt's Terminal List future offers more details on what's ahead.

Part of the show's appeal comes from Pratt's performance as Reece, a character who is forced to navigate the aftermath of extreme violence while trying to determine who he can trust. The series also benefits from its grounded military details and willingness to make its action sequences central to the story rather than simply using them as background spectacle.

The franchise has continued to develop since its first season, with its second installment giving Reece another chapter in his story. The Terminal List season 2's Rotten Tomatoes score offers another look at how the latest episodes have been received, adding a critical perspective to the show's continued streaming performance.

Carr's work also gives Prime Video plenty of material to explore beyond Reece's story. The author has developed a larger collection of military thrillers, and viewers interested in similar adaptations will soon be able to tune in to a new detective series with a military twist called Worth in the works.

A Navy SEAL commander returns home after a disastrous covert mission leaves his entire platoon dead, only to find conflicting memories and growing evidence of a far reaching conspiracy. When tragedy strikes his family, grief turns to determination as he hunts those responsible, uncovering corruption that reaches deep into the military, government, and intelligence communities.

Amazon has dropped the Bose Smart Ultra Soundbar to $649 from its usual $999, taking $350 off and bringing it to the lowest price we've seen so far, according to price trackers. PCMag rated the Smart Ultra "outstanding," highlighting its ability to deliver surprisingly immersive Dolby Atmos audio without requiring a room full of additional speakers. If you don't need Bose's top-tier model, there's a less expensive option as well: the Bose Smart Dolby Atmos Soundbar ($399, down from $429), which sits below the Smart Ultra in the lineup.

The Smart Ultra uses a 5.1.2-channel design with nine drivers, including two upward-firing drivers that bounce sound off the ceiling to create height effects. In practice, that means movies, TV shows, and games feel larger and more spacious than they do through most single-bar setups. Bose also includes its AdaptiQ room-calibration system, which measures your room's acoustics and adjusts the sound accordingly. The process takes a few minutes, but it helps the soundbar perform better across different spaces rather than relying on a one-size-fits-all tuning profile. The soundbar also works as a smart speaker, with Amazon Alexa built in and support for Apple AirPlay 2, Google Cast, Spotify Connect, Bluetooth, and multi-room audio through the Bose app.

Its biggest compromise is bass—for a single soundbar, its low end is respectable, but it can't fully replace what a dedicated subwoofer brings to action movies, concerts, or bass-heavy music. The good news is that Bose allows you to expand the system later with compatible wireless subwoofers and surround speakers if you decide you want more impact. For anyone looking for a premium one-piece soundbar that delivers convincing Dolby Atmos effects, clear dialogue, built-in smart features, and a much larger soundstage than TV speakers can provide, the Smart Ultra remains one of the strongest standalone options available, especially at this price.

The winter air-drying rules that actually cut your laundry drying time in half

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

When cold, wet weather rolls in, drying laundry indoors without a clothes dryer often turns into a multi-day ordeal. Piles of damp fabric draped across clothes airers bring chilling humidity into your living space, leaving garments smelling stale and walls prone to condensation and mould.

The secret to slashing indoor drying times lies not in cranking up the central heating to full blast, but in mastering air movement, extraction, and strategic placement. Here is how to dry your clothes indoors quickly and cleanly this winter, without inviting damp, mold, or musty smells into your home.

The single most effective shortcut begins before your clothes even leave the washing machine drum. Most spin cycles leave substantial moisture trapped deep inside thick cottons, heavy jeans, and knitwear.

Running a dedicated second spin cycle at your machine’s maximum spin speed pulls out surprising amounts of excess water without adding heat or risking fabric damage.

Shaking each item out vigorously immediately after unloading loosens compacted fibres and opens up airflow pockets that otherwise trap dampness for hours.

Where and how you hang wet laundry makes the difference between fresh clothes in hours and musty garments after two days. Cramming items closely onto a clothes drying rack restricts air circulation, trapping damp air directly between layers of fabric.

If you can, space each garment across two rungs rather than one, or slip button-up shirts and tops onto sturdy coat hangers suspended along the outer frame to keep fabrics exposed to circulating room air.

Moisture evaporates only as fast as the surrounding air can absorb and carry it away. Trapping a full airer in a closed, cold room creates a humid microclimate that halts evaporation entirely.

Positioning your clothes airer roughly a foot away from a heating duct, never draped directly in front of it, which blocks heating efficiency and risks scorching fabrics, paired with an oscillating fan on its lowest setting forces air constantly across the textiles.

If your home struggles with persistent condensation in late fall and winter, running one of the best dehumidifiers directly beneath or alongside the rack draws pints of moisture straight out of the wet fibres while blowing warm, dry air back through the load.

#3272. Apple announces Fitness+ Gym Strength program with personalized workout plans

Apple wants to help you get stronger. Apple Fitness+ is expanding to the gym with a new strength training experience. Gym Strength is now available in beta, bringing personalized workout plans, exercise demonstrations, and Apple Watch logging to your lifting routine.

Gym Strength creates progressive, four-week plans based on your strength goals, experience, schedule, and available equipment. After you complete each week of workouts, the following week adapts based on the reps and weight you logged.

The feature is designed for a range of experience levels, from people trying strength training for the first time to experienced lifters looking to make progress. It also aims to help anyone who wants to build a more consistent routine.

When building a plan, you choose your workout days and the body areas you want to focus on. You can select five exercises per workout, which Apple estimates will take about 20–30 minutes, or seven exercises for about 45–60 minutes, depending on your pace.

Each workout recommends exercises, reps, sets, and how much weight to lift.

You move through the workout at your own pace, with short video demonstrations from Apple Fitness+ trainers available for each exercise. The demonstrations can be expanded to show the movement from three different angles.

Apple says Gym Strength includes over 350 exercises across more than 30 types of strength training equipment, including dumbbells, kettlebells, suspension trainers, cable machines, and barbells. Dumbbells are the minimum equipment requirement.

Plans account for the equipment available to you, so the experience can work in a commercial gym or a home gym.

If a machine is occupied or you’re training somewhere with different equipment, you can swap equipment or choose an alternative exercise with a similar movement and body focus. You can also add sets or skip exercises.

Gym Strength requires an iPhone running iOS 27.3 or an iPad running iPadOS 27.3. An Apple Watch running watchOS 27.3 optionally lets you view exercises and log reps and weight from your wrist, while tracking heart rate and calories burned.

Gym Strength also introduces Training Note, an optional feature powered by Apple Intelligence that previews workouts, explains progression, and highlights milestones. Training Note requires an Apple Intelligence–enabled iPhone or iPad with the device set to English.

Gym Strength is included in the existing Fitness+ subscription. It joins a library of trainer-led workouts spanning 12 workout types, including Strength, HIIT, Yoga, Pilates, Core, Cycling, Rowing, Dance, Kickboxing, treadmill walking and running, and Mindful Cooldown.

Fitness+ also offers guided meditations, personalized recommendations, and Custom Plans for scheduling workouts, with new sessions added every week.

Fitness+ is also included in Apple One Premier, which costs $39.95 per month in the U.S. and bundles Apple Music, Apple TV, Apple Arcade, Apple News+, and 2TB of iCloud+ storage.

#3271. The Top 10 Movies Right Now, According to Streaming Data

The most streamed movie in October was Steven Spielberg's Disclosure Day, but half of the month's top ten is made up of season-appropriate horror movies. This year's two most successful horror movies, Backrooms and Obsession, made the list; so did a classic (Halloween from 1978) and an art movie about the genre that Halloween created,Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma. Perfect double feature. Rounding out the list is the all-around-excellent Hokum. If you're not into horror, you might like Golden Arm, a comedy that refused to die, star-studded comedy The Invite, or ultimate crowd-pleaser Project Hail Mary.

Legendary director Steven Spielberg returns to the extraterrestrials he loves so much with a thriller that's a spiritual sequel to Close Encounters of the Third Kind. Disclosure Day details the events that lead up to the revelation that aliens are among us. Josh O’Connor plays Dr. Daniel Kellner, a cybersecurity expert for a government contractor who uncovers explosive evidence that his employers would kill to keep secret. Meanwhile, a TV meteorologist (Emily Blunt) begins speaking in an alien language. It all sets the stage for a series of set pieces and chases leading to the biggest revelation in human history. Stream Disclosure Day on Peacock.

Director Kane Parsons' analog horror breakthrough is proof that atmosphere, mood, and a fascinating story is scarier than CGI monsters every time. Based on the viral YouTube series of the same name, Backrooms tells the story of Clark (Chiwetel Ejiofor), a store owner who discovers a labyrinthian liminal space in his furniture shop's basement. Renate Reinsve plays his therapist, who goes downstairs for a visit and does not find it easy to return. A hit with critics—Backrooms is sitting at 86% fresh on Rotten Tomatoes—and audiences, Backrooms is a delicious Halloween treat for horror fans. Stream Backrooms on HBO Max.

Director Curry Barker is still in his 20s, but his debut theatrical feature is the kind of horror film that changes the entire genre. Obsession is a classic "be careful what you wish for" story that feels fresh thanks to its talented young cast, unpredictable plot, and careful pace. Michael Johnston plays a young man too scared to tell his crush how he feels, so he wishes she'd fall in love with him instead. The result is a nightmare embodied by Inde Navarrette, whose portrayal of the villain/victim is at once harrowing, terrifying, and heartbreaking. Obsession is the best horror movie I've seen in years. Stream Obsession on Peacock.

This comedy-drama from A24 is packed with heavy-hitting actors. Olivia Wilde, who also directed the film, plays Angela, and Seth Rogen plays her husband, Joe. With the straight-laced couple's marriage on thin ice, Angela and Joe invite their more, uh, open-minded neighbors Piña, played by Penélope Cruz, and Hawk, played by Edward Norton, over for dinner. The evening unravels in hilarious ways, changing everyone's life. If you're a fan of smart, honest comedy, you will really like The Invite. Stream The Invite on HBO Max.

With Hokum, Director Damian McCarthy (Oddity, Caveat) carefully builds a suffocatingly creepy story around Adam Scott's portrayal of Ohm Bauman, a celebrity novelist and unmitigated jerk who travels to the isolated Bilberry Woods Hotel in Ireland to scatter the ashes of his parents and finish his book. Bauman soon learns that the lore of the hotel includes an ancient witch who feeds her victims to the creatures of hell, and she might be more than just a local legend. Hokum is a horror movie for fans of dreadful atmosphere and careful pacing instead of gore or jump-scares. Stream Hokum on Hulu.

With a title like this, it's not going to be a normal movie. Director Jane Schoenbrun’s I Saw the TV Glow and We're All Going to the World's Fair are two of the most fascinating, fiercely original horror movies of the last decade, and their third film follows in those strange footfalls. While it's technically a meta re-imagining of the slasher genre, Miasma goes way deeper than Scream ever could. It's a postmodern exploration of why the slasher genre's cocktail of sex, death, and subversion casts such a strong spell on interesting, weird people. Definitely see this movie. Stream Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma on Mubi.

When Golden Arm was released in 2021, not many people paid attention—with the pandemic in full swing, people didn't seem to have room for a quirky, indie comedy about a woman's quest to win the ladies' arm-wrestling championship—but it's a new age, and you should stream Golden Arm. It's sitting on a perfect score at Rotten Tomatoes, the movie's stars, Mary Holland and Betsy Sodaro, are charming and hilarious, and you can catch Golden Arm on Fandango, a free streaming service. What's not to love? Stream Golden Arm on Fandango or Prime Video.

In this crowd-pleasing sci-fi flick, Ryan Gosling stars as Ryland Grace, a middle school science teacher who is blasted into the firmament in a last-ditch effort to save the world. Grace is the only person on Earth who might know how to protect the sun from a cosmic infection that threatens all life, but he's definitely not an astronaut and doesn't see himself as a hero either. Will he rise to the occasion and learn something about his inner strength and resilience while saving us all from death? My money is on, "yeah, probably." Stream Project Hail Mary on MGM+, Prime Video, and Philo.

Hundreds of slasher movies have been released since Halloween came out in 1978, but none have surpassed the original. Michael Myers' expressionless visage and the synthesizer theme have become universally recognized cultural signifiers for "horror movie," and every shot in Halloween has been stolen countless times, but the movie is so good, it's still scary. Watch or re-watch Halloween now! Stream Halloween on Philo, AMC+, and Prime Video.

Directed by and starring Ben Affleck, Animals is a thriller that tells the story of Mark Kimball, a Los Angeles mayoral candidate whose son is kidnapped and held for ransom. Having spent every dime on his outsider campaign, Kimball is forced to turn to extreme methods to guarantee his son's safe return, even if it conflicts with his public persona as a man of the people. Animals is a taut, expertly directed movie that should more than satisfy fans of political thrillers. Stream Animals on Netflix.

#3270. iOS 27.3 adds all-new Apple Health app, details here

Apple released iOS 27.3 beta 1 today, and it reintroduces the all-new Health app that was first available for testing during the iOS 27.2 beta. Here’s what’s new.

iOS 27.3 will launch with an upgraded Apple Health app. The new app was initially tested during the iOS 27.2 beta, but it’s back today in iOS 27.3 beta 1 and will ship to all users next month.

Today on Apple Newsroom, the company outlined what to expect from the new Health experience.

Three central new Health features are highlighted for iOS 27.3:

Insights tab: “surfaces timely, holistic summaries spanning heart, sleep, readiness, fitness, vitals, and cycle tracking data throughout the day. A dedicated For You section delivers intelligent recommendations tailored to a user’s daily habits — such as practical guidance to adjust a wind-down routine following consecutive nights of interrupted sleep. The app pairs data with dynamic health content, offering educational videos and articles featuring Health app clinical experts.”

Longevity tab: “analyzes longitudinal metrics across heart health, sleep, mental wellbeing, movement, metabolic health, hearing, and nutrition. Central to this tab is Health Age, a feature that translates data from Apple Watch — including VO2 max, resting heart rate, sleep, and heart rate variability — into a metric that reflects how a user’s body is tracking relative to their chronological age. Users can also incorporate clinical laboratory data, such as A1c and LDL cholesterol, to enrich their long-term health picture.”

At-home movement evaluations: “make physical assessments accessible without requiring specialized equipment. Using an iPhone camera and Apple Watch, users can measure their flexibility, strength, balance, movement mechanics, and VO2 max with real-time audio and visual feedback. Powered by on-device vision-based AI models and developed with clinical experts, the experience runs entirely on device; no video is ever recorded, stored, or shared.“

Additionally, Apple says that the new Health app offers expanded language support. It is available in global English, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), French, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

What do you think of the new Health app in iOS 27.3? Let us know in the comments.

#3269. Kevin Costner's Forgotten 117-Minute Action Thriller Is Mandatory Viewing on HBO Max

While he has been one of the biggest names in entertainment for more than four decades, Kevin Costner isn't immune to his movies getting overlooked by audiences. Just a couple of years ago, his long-awaited Western project Horizon: An American Saga totally bombed at the box office, putting the film's planned sequels on hold. Not every movie can be Dances With Wolves or Bull Durham, and a couple are going to slip through the cracks every now and again.

Such is the fate of a 12-year-old thriller that starred Costner as an international spy battling brain cancer. 3 Days to Kill, directed by Charlie's Angels helmer McG, was released in 2014 to mixed reviews and a less-than-stellar box office performance. More than a decade later, however, the thriller is streaming on HBO Max, where it is looking to capture a new audience, and remind folks of how consistently great Costner has been over the years.

When it first hit theaters back in 2014, 3 Days to Kill made just over $53 million at the global box office. That's not the worst result imaginable, considering its production was right around $28 million, but suffice it to say the film didn't really latch on with audiences. A lot of folks, even major Costner fans, missed out on the thriller the first time around, leaving it up to home media releases and streaming to help it build an audience over time.

3 Days to Kill isn't the best of its genre — not by a long shot — but it does feel like the kind of movie that would've easily found a following at Blockbusters or on cable reruns back in the day. It's very much an afternoon TNT kind of flick. Now, with streaming lineups as filled to the brim as they are, a film like this is a little harder to discover. That said, it's kind of the perfect rainy day or late night watch on HBO Max, especially with its stacked cast that will keep your attention throughout.

If you're one of the many who missed 3 Days to Kill over the years, it's the same kind of thriller you've seen a bunch of times before, but with a few fresh wrinkles and a pretty great cast. Costner stars as Ethan Renner, a CIA operative who has discovered that he's dying of brain cancer. With the sickness changing his entire outlook on life, his new focus is on getting out of the spy game and fixing his relationship with his estranged wife and teenage daughter. While spending time with said daughter, he's given a final job — a job he only takes because the payment includes an experimental drug that could potentially save his life. Renner now has to navigate the tangled web of a dangerous international conspiracy while also protecting his daughter, who is now accidentally caught up in the mess as well.

Costner was obviously the big draw for 3 Days to Kill, but he's one of several notable stars in the cast. Connie Nielsen plays his wife, while Hailee Steinfeld co-stars as their daughter. The film also stars Amber Heard as a fellow agent in the CIA, as well as Justified's Raymond J. Barry, who plays the CIA director.

#3268. At Last, The MCU Is Officially Setting Up The Best Doctor Doom/Scarlet Witch Story

Marvel Studios is preparing for the debut of Robert Downey Jr.s Doctor Doom in Avengers: Doomsday, which is set to release at the end of this year. However, an exciting new theory suggests Doom's arrival in the MCU may also involve the return of The Scarlet Witch.

Played by Elizabeth Olsen, Wanda Maximoff's Scarlet Witch has been absent from the main MCU continuity since 2022's Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, which saw Wanda controversially being corrupted by the Darkhold in a bid to reunite with her sons from a different reality (no matter the cost). Eventually, Wanda was shown how far she'd fallen, prompting her to sacrifice herself by bringing down Mount Wundagore, destroying every copy of the Darkhold in the process.

That said, many fans have never stopped believing in Wanda's eventual return to the MCU, especially with the rest of her family still having such prominent, ongoing roles. Between the new VisionQuest series on Disney+ and the reveal of mysterious mystical characters beyond Victor von Doom in Avengers: Doomsday, there's plenty reason to suspect that Marvel Studios has secret plans for the Scarlet Witch (which may involve Doctor Doom himself).

Beginning with 2021's WandaVision, Wanda's grief losing Vision (Paul Bettany) in Avengers: Infinity War led to her inadvertent creation of a massive hex over the town of Westview, transforming it into her TV-perfect happy ending, while also manifesting a new Vision and their twin boys from the comics, Billy and Tommy. By the end of WandaVision, Wanda undid the hex despite the fact it meant losing Vision and here boys. This is what ultimately led to her corruption by the Darkhold trying to get her boys back via another reality and subsequent death at Mount Wundagore in 2022's Multiverse of Madness.

However, the story of Wanda Maximoff's family has very much continued even without Wanda herself. In 2024's Agatha All Along, it was revealed that Billy used his magic to transfer his soul into the body of teenager William Kaplan (Joe Locke) before the Hex was being undone. He then did the same for Tommy's soul with Thomas Shepherd (Ruaridh Mollica), a key parallel to their origins from the comics.

While Agatha All Along ended with Billy/William and the ghost of Agatha Harkness searching for Tommy/Thomas, we now have 2026's VisionQuest starring the original Vision (rebuilt by SWORD at the end of WandaVision), as well as Tommy himself who's gradually been learning from his synthezoid "father" about Wanda, the events of Westview, and their family.

With VisionQuest just days away from its finale, Vision and the Maximoff twins finding each other again feels increasingly likely. Combined with Vision starting to regain the humanity and emotion he temporarily lost after being reactivated, nearly all of the pieces are in place for a major Maximoff family reunion in the MCU's future except one: Wanda.

While she seemed to have died under the collapse of Mount Wundagore, The Scarlet Witch is one of the most powerful beings in the entire Marvel Universe. As such, it's not much of a leap in logic to suggest that she could have survived (or was perhaps even rescued by someone seeking her power...)

Beyond what's been happening on the small-screen for the surviving Maximoffs, the ambiguity and hopes about Wanda's return have never been higher thanks to Avengers: Doomsday and its masked "Latverian Witches" who will apparently be serving Doctor Doom.

Their exact identities and purpose of these witches in the upcoming MCU crossover have yet to be confirmed, and they may very well just be generic servants of Doom (a master sorcerer in his own right). However, they've notably been shown wearing different colored robes including green, purple, orange, and red, leading many to wonder if established magical characters like Sylvie, Agatha, Clea, or Wanda herself could be under Doom's influence.

Choose the movie with the higher Rotten Tomatoes score.

Thinking about Wanda in particular, Doom would have certainly had the power to secretly intervene to save Wanda at Mount Wundagore, perhaps in a bid to bring her into his service and plans for the multiverse at large. There's also some key comics precedent for this idea as well, as seen in Marvel's classic "Children's Crusade" storyline.

In "Children's Crusade", Doctor Doom secretly takes in an amnesiac Wanda from Mount Wundagore after her major breakdown that resulted in her magic triggering the near-genocide of mutantkind (House of M). Hoping to marry Wanda and use her power for his own ends, the intervention of Wanda's boys, their fellow Young Avengers, and several Avengers and X-Men alike prevented Doom from taking full control of the Scarlet Witch's power and her memories being restored.

While none of this confirms that the MCU's Wanda Maximoff is indeed one of these Latverian Witches in Doomsday, being onee of the masked magic wielders would provide a very natural way for the MCU to kick-off a new storyline inspired by "Children's Crusade", perhaps even one that continues beyond the Multiverse Saga itself.

The basic premise of "Children's Crusade" feels remarkably perfect to the MCU's future. While VisionQuest can bring Billy and Tommy together with Vision, Avengers: Doomsday can establish Doom's true purpose for these Latverian Witches, and whether one of them is indeed Wanda Maximoff. Perhaps the reveal will even saved for the end of Doomsday or even in 2027's Avengers: Secret Wars to then kick off a substantial project in the MCU's next major saga.

Most importantly, this major MCU thoery would go a long way to redeem the events of Multiverse of Madness and Wanda's controversial (and underveloped) turn to the darkness. Likewise, throwing Doctor Doom into the mix even just to start would not only keep the Maximoff Family's story tied to the greater events happening in the MCU, but would also provide the perfect narrative launchpad by adapting the basic elements from "Children's Crusade".

It may be some time before we get it, but the twins' reunion more than likely approaching and Doctor Doom's mysterious magical followers definitely makes it feel like a solid foundation is being formed for Wanda's long hoped-for return in the MCU.

The finale of VisionQuest begins streaming November 10th on Disney+. Avengers: Doomsday releases in theaters on December 18th from Marvel Studios.

Have you recently checked out a certain Irishman's latest action-thriller involving a combat veteran? Then you’re likely keen to revisit some of Liam Neeson’s past action work. I’ve got you covered on that front. Cold, charismatic and with an iconic accent that could melt steel, how can you not love this actor’s stellar CV?

I’ve adored Liam ever since I first saw him in 1995’s “Rob Roy”, even if his Highland accent isn’t the best. Hey, I’m Scottish (I can judge). Over the last 20 years of tackling terrorists and timber wolves, Neeson has become a slightly unlikely action star. After all, how many performers can claim to be an actual Jedi who has also starred in a Steven Spielberg Best Picture winner? ‘One’ is the answer. His name is Liam Neeson, and here are three action movies you need to watch after seeing “The Mongoose”.

Ah yes, the film that alerted the world to Mr. Nesson’s “very particular set of skills”. Said skills happen to include beating bad guys rotten, should they be silly enough to kidnap Big Liam’s daughter. Though it seems bizarre to say, considering he played the main role in 1993’s widely acclaimed “Schindler’s List”, 2008’s “Taken” does feel like the iconic North Irishman’s most pivotal part.

However “The Mongoose” ultimately performs at the box office, you could argue the main reason Neeson’s latest project exists is because of “Taken”. In playing a vengeful father capable of kicking serious ass well into middle age, Liam laid down the blueprint for 20 years’ worth of solid action work. This thriller pinned Neeson as the go-to hard guy with a heart. He’s deservedly lived well off that image ever since.

Watch "Taken" on Prime Video (buy/rent) now

Let me paint you a picture: Liam Neeson vs wolves. That’s it. You’re either in or you’re out… and you should definitely be in. The premise is semi-absurd — Neeson’s refinery worker survives a plane crash in Alaska then has to beat up fluffy timber predators — but “The Grey” totally works as a no-frills ‘guilty pleasure’ movie. Don’t let anyone ever judge you for enjoying Liam kicking CGI wolves to the turf.

Admittedly, said effects haven’t aged that well. Hollywood continues to have a problem nailing down convincing CG fur. Still, that shouldn't put you off this chilly thriller. The whole reason the movie works is because Neeson treats proceedings with his trademark sense of unironic gravitas. When he kicks a computer-generated canine in the face, you know he believes it. After the all-timer that is 1981’s “American Werewolf in London”, this is definitely my second favorite lupine flick.

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

Watch "The Grey on Prime Video (buy/rent) now

The Year of our Lord 2011 was a big one for Mr. Neeson. Qui-Gon Jinn really enjoyed getting into crashes over this 12 month period (see “The Grey” above). A handsome man who is at least six feet and four inches tall shouldn’t be able to play a low-key doctor so well, but that’s Jedi mind tricks for you. Hollywood has seen Neeson as an every man for a couple of decades now, even in real life you know the actor could slay you with an upper eyebrow.

A Berlin-set tale of stolen identities, there’s a hint of Hitchcock classic “North by Northwest” about this Neeson thriller; even if the film takes itself more seriously than Alfred’s iconic dark comedy. The convenient "Amnesia Effect” trope is admittedly on the nose, but Neeson plays out the action with his typified class. It’s no "Schindler's List”, but "Unknown" is still worth 113 minutes of your time.

#3266. iOS 27.3 and macOS 27.3 add Vertical Tabs, Adaptive Dark Mode, and more to Safari

Apple just released the first betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3, with some big changes to Safari. The updates add a new vertical tab layout, Adaptive Dark Mode, and Siri AI Custom Actions.

Safari in iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3 is adding a new Vertical Tabs design option. If you choose this design, you’ll see your tabs arranged vertically along the left-hand side of Safari rather than along the top, as in the traditional Safari design.

By default, Vertical Tabs show as icons in order to maximize vertical and horizontal space. If you’d like, you can also resize the tab bar to see website titles.

To try Vertical Tabs in the new iOS 27.3 beta, head to the Settings app, choose Apps, tap Safari, then look for the new Vertical Tabs option. On Mac and iPad, the feature can also be enabled via the “View” menu in the Safari app directly.

Vertical tab layouts have become an increasingly popular web browser feature. Arc from The Browser Company popularized the option. Arc, however, ceased development last year, and The Browser Company announced last month that it will discontinue it altogether in December.

If you regularly visit a website that doesn’t support Dark Mode, Apple’s next round of software updates adds Adaptive Dark Mode. This will automatically apply Dark Mode to websites that don’t support the feature.

If Dark Mode is enabled on your iPhone, iPad, or Mac and you visit a website that doesn’t support it, you’ll see a new “Try” button. If you tap this, Safari will automatically create a Dark Mode version of the website.

You can choose to have Adaptive Dark Mode automatically kick in or use it on a site-by-site basis.

Finally, Siri AI can now take direct action on tabs in iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3. This includes things like using Siri to move, sort, organize, and close your tabs.

In a future update, Siri’s on-screen awareness will also expand to include the entire content of a website, not just what’s visible on the screen at a particular moment.

iOS 27.3, macOS 27.3, and iPadOS 27.3 are rolling out to developers for beta testing today. The update will likely be released to everyone sometime in December. What do you think of these new Safari features? Will you try out the new Vertical Tabs feature? Let us know down in the comments.

#3265. The Top 10 TV Series Right Now, According to Streaming Data

October's ten most-streamed series are packed with your future favorite shows. There's a couple of modernizations of horror franchises for Halloween (Carrie and Crystal Lake), as well as new horror series Below and Phony. There's an excellent new superhero series Lanterns, sprawling family drama East of Eden, and new seasons of favorites Ted Lasso, Slow Horses, The Diplomat, and Mobland. So don't even try to tell anyone there's nothing on.

Horror master Mike Flanagan (Haunting of Hill House, Midnight Mass) re-imagines Stephen King's tale of teenage telekinesis, taking the story from the 1970s to now, complete with cyber bullying, smart phones, and a modern sensibility. The core of the tale, though, remains the same, as does the titular character's bloody coming-of-age. Powered by a talented young cast that includes Siena Agudong as Susan and Summer H. Howell as the title character, Carrie is a trick-or-treat for horror fans. Stream Carrie on Prime.

Based on John Steinbeck's pillar of Western literature, East of Eden follows three generations of the hardscrabble Hamilton family and the upscale Trask family, farming and ranching clans in California's Salinas Valley. The show's production is a multigenerational story too: It was written and created by Zoe Kazan, whose grandpa Elia directed the 1955 film version of East of Eden. All respect to Elia Kazan, but Steinbeck's story is so massive, it needs a seven-part mini-series. East of Eden is the kind of sprawling, melodramatic story that episodic television was made for. Stream East of Eden on Netflix.

Like Carrie, Crystal Lake reimagines a horror classic—in this case, Friday the 13th—and expands the lore even beyond the 12 films in the franchise. If you've ever wondered how Pamela Voorhees, played here by Linda Cardellini, became a serial murderer, and how her son Jason ended up a relentless, camp-counselor-killing-machine who lives at the bottom of a lake, Crystal Lake has all the answers. In a lot of ways, this show is better than all of the movies. Stream Crystal Lake on Peacock.

Apple TV's Slow Horses delivers a realistic, nuanced take on espionage by detailing the lives of the losers of British Intelligence. Instead of chiseled good guys and gals saving the world, the agents of Slough House are a team of dysfunctional, troubled souls trying to do the right thing (usually) in a morally gray world, just like real agents. Their leader, gruff, obnoxious Jackson Lamb, is played to perfection by Gary Oldman. Slow Horses has an almost perfect Rotten Tomatoes score over its first five seasons, and season 6 is setting new records. Stream Slow Horses on Apple TV+.

DC's TV revamp of Green Lantern details what happens when experienced Lantern Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) trains the new guy, John Stewart (Aaron Pierre), on how to wield the mysterious and powerful Green Lantern Ring. It's a reserved, neo-noir style take on the comic mythos, as the heroes investigate a series of murders tied to an extraterrestrial threat. Lanterns is pulling in a better than 90% fresh ratings from Rotten Tomatoes, so it's definitely worth a stream. Stream Lanterns on HBO Max.

Created by Jesse McKeown and starring Josh Hartnett, Charlie Heaton, and Mackenzie Davis, Below is set in a Newfoundland fishing village beset with aquatic horror. When the Canadian government offers the residents of Snooks Arm a ton of money to relocate, no one really knows why, but ice fisherman Calvin Penney (Hartnett) suspects it has something to do with the monster he saw under the ice when he was a child. If you like taut creature feature style horror, check out Below. Stream Below on Netflix.

Season four of Ted Lasso sees the title character, played by Jason Sudeikis, returning to the UK to take on a new challenge: coaching the Lady Greyhounds, AFC Richmond's second-division women's football team. This multiple Emmy Award-winning series still has all the heart, humor, and positivity of the original run. Stream Ted Lasso on Apple TV+.

The mystery that drives creepy coming-of-age drama Phony is killer: Sonny Cooke, played by Sam Nivola, is a teenager with a very close relationship to his devoted single mother Ellen, played by Connie Britton. After a freak car accident, he wakes up convinced that his mom is an impostor. She looks the same, but there's something off about her in a way that Sonny can't describe, so he sets out to solve the mystery. Phony is rated over 90% fresh on Rotten Tomatoes. Stream Phony on Hulu.

In season four of political thriller series The Diplomat, the Kate Wyler, played by Keri Russell, finds that diplomatic relations between the U.S. and the UK are starting to crumble, and so is her marriage. Meanwhile, U.S. president Grace Penn, played by Allison Janney, and VP Hal Wyler, played by Rufus Sewell, continue their conspiracy to steal a Russian super-weapon, nudging the nation toward war with our longtime adversary. In other words, it's an international mess, with a few powerful people keeping the world from descending into chaos. If you like political intrigue, this is the series for you. Stream The Diplomat on Netflix.

Who doesn't love a sprawling organized crime drama? In Mobland, the crime is being organized in Great Britain, where two warring London crime families, the Harrigans and Stevensons, are locked in a battle for underworld power. In the middle of the crossfire is Harry Da Souza, a gritty fixer played to gruff perfection by Tom Hardy. Season 2 finds Da Souza in the unenviable position of holding together the Harrigan family on the verge of civil war. If you like backstabbing, scheming, murder, and other tropes of high-stakes crime thrillers, you'll like Mobland. Stream Mobland on Paramount+.

#3264. watchOS 27.3 beta adds new Siri Recap and Live Rewind features for Apple Watch

Apple has released the first beta of watchOS 27.3 for developers, including two new Audio Intelligence features for Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4: Siri Recap and Live Rewind.

Apple first announced these features at its special event in September, saying they would “arrive in beta later this year.”

As a refresher, Siri Recap creates high-level summaries of conversations that you can review later. When the feature is enabled, Apple Intelligence will automatically generate a title and key points that you can review in the Siri app on iPhone.

Siri Recap ambiently takes notes on your conversations throughout your day and creates high-level Apple Intelligence–generated summaries that you can use later to jog your memory, so you can stay present in the moment. Your summaries auto-delete after 7 days if you choose not to save them.

You can turn on Siri Recap in the Watch app on iPhone. When you enable it, you can set a schedule based on time and/or location, or you can manually turn it on or off. You can also access it via Control Center on Apple Watch.

Live Rewind, meanwhile, helps you recall what was just said in a conversation. You can activate Live Rewind by double-pressing the Digital Crown, and then see a transcript of the previous 15 seconds of a conversation.

Live Rewind recalls what was just said in the last 15 seconds by showing a text snippet on your Apple Watch when you double-press the Digital Crown, so you can catch something you missed or are less familiar with. You can ask Siri about the content of the snippet or simply save it to the Siri app.

Siri Recap’s summary is described as a “brief, high-level summary of conversations,” not a transcript. Apple says it will “exclude sensitive information like financial information or government-assigned identifiers.”

Live Rewind text snippets and Siri Recap summaries are end-to-end encrypted. Apple says the features “do not create or store audio recordings, and raw audio used for processing is completely inaccessible to the operating systems, apps, the user, or Apple.” The company uses the S11 chip’s Secure Exclave to power the features, a “dedicated hardware-isolated compartment that processes audio in complete isolation from the rest of the system, then immediately deletes it.”

Siri Recap and Live Rewind are available in beta with watchOS 27.3, which is available now for developers.

#3263. I ran 35 miles in the Salomon Aero Blaze 4 GRVL GTX, and it’s a great waterproof shoe for mixed terrain running

The Salomon Aero Blaze 4 GRVL GTX is a waterproof running shoe designed primarily for gravel, but it’s also very capable on roads and other light trails. It will suit some runners’ needs perfectly, but the waterproof upper can run hot.

Comfortable midsole with good energy return

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

For those of us in the Northern Hemisphere, the cold, wet days of winter are approaching fast, and if you plan on running through the season, there are some benefits to buying a specialist set of running shoes for it.

The two features I look for in the best running shoes for the winter are an outsole that grips well in wet conditions and a water-repellent or waterproof upper.

Both boxes are ticked by the Salomon Aero Blaze 4 GRVL GTX, which has a Gore-Tex membrane in the upper, is fully waterproof, and has a gravel-ready outsole that works well on a wide variety of terrain.

I’ve used the shoe for a mix of runs on roads, light trails and grassy hills and it’s impressed me as a winter-ready daily trainer. If you don’t need its waterproof upper or versatile outsole, though, you’ll get a better ride from some lighter, bouncier road options like the Asics Novablast 6.

The Salomon Aero Blaze 4 GRVL GTX launched in fall 2026 and costs $160 in the U.S. and £145 in the U.K., which is $20/£20 more expensive than the standard model of the shoe without the Gore-Tex upper.

Salomon also released the Aero Glide 4 GRVL in its line-up, which is a slightly softer and more cushioned option than the Blaze, which some runners might prefer for easy long runs in particular.

The Aero Blaze 4 GRVL GTX is currently available in four colors, including Vanilla Ice, the model I tested for those who want to show off the dirt they run through, and an all-black design for those who don’t.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

My US men’s size 10 weighs exactly 10oz, which is light for a shoe with a thick outsole, waterproof upper, and tall stack of foam in the midsole.

The stack height is 37mm at the heel and 29mm at the forefoot for an 8mm drop, which is a little lower than the stack on the Aero Glide 4 GRVL.

I found the shoe fit me well in my normal running shoe size, and the Gore-Tex upper wasn’t stiff or uncomfortable during my testing.

The Aero Blaze 4 GRVL GTX uses a mesh upper with Gore-Tex lining and padding on the tongue and around the collar.

During my testing, I was able to run in heavy rain and splash through puddles without my feet getting wet, and I also like that it’s quick and easy to clean the waterproof upper after muddy runs.

However, the drawback is that it’s not the most breathable material, and when running in warm conditions or using the shoe for walks, my feet got sweatier than normal.

Rather than traditional laces, it has Salomon’s QuickLace Neo system so you can loosen and tighten the fit quickly with the pull toggle, which you can then tuck under an elastic band so it doesn’t bounce around on the run.

The Aero Blaze 4 GRVL GTX uses a supercritical TPU foam called OptiFoam Squared in its midsole, with a mild rocker shape helping to roll you from heel to toe with each stride.

I’m a fan of this foam, which is also used on the Aero Glide 4 GRVL. It’s soft enough to be comfortable without being overly squishy, and it gives a good amount of energy return when you hit faster paces.

The rubber outsole on the shoe has 2.5mm deep, chevron-shaped lugs that are built to grip on gravel tracks but also work well on roads and other light trails.

This outsole is a star feature on the shoe because it allows you to tackle such a wide variety of terrain with confidence, even in wet conditions.

The Salomon Aero Blaze 4 GRVL GTX proved to be an enjoyably versatile shoe in my testing. I used it as my main daily trainer, tackling easy, steady-paced runs mainly on the road and forest trails.

I also used it for one run on slightly more technical trails with rocky and grassy sections, and throughout all my testing, the grip was impressively reliable, even in very wet conditions. It’s not a good option for deep mud, but can handle most other trails well.

That versatility extends to the paces the Aero Blaze 4 GRVL GTX can handle. The midsole has a responsive feel at faster paces while soft enough for long, easy runs — it felt good at all the paces I’d run at outside dedicated interval workouts.

The waterproof upper does its job on rainy days well, and also helps keep your feet warm on easy runs in cold conditions.

However, this upper did limit me because it can be a bit too hot at times. My feet got very sweaty on longer runs on dry days, and if you’re a runner who uses one shoe for everything, a fully waterproof sneaker like this probably isn't the best buy.

The Salomon Aero Blaze 4 GRVL GTX does a great job in the role it’s built for. The waterproof upper is great on wet, cold days; the outsole grips well in wet and dry conditions on both the road and light trails, and the midsole is enjoyably energetic.

If that all sounds good but you want something a little softer and more cushioned, the Salomon Aero Glide 4 GRVL also comes in a Gore-Tex model, and Salomon also has non-GTX models of both shoes, and road versions with less substantial outsoles.

There are a lot of choices in the line-up, and I’d say all are good shoes thanks to the OptiFoam Squared midsole at the heart of them, so you can tailor your Blaze or Glide to suit your needs and preferences.

If you’re sticking to the roads during your winter runs, I’d also consider the Adidas Adizero Evo SL ATR, which has a water-repellent upper and small lugs on its outsole. It’s a good option if the full waterproof upper and thick outsole on the Aero Blaze 4 GRVL GTX is overkill for your needs.

#3262. This New Chrome AI Feature Reads Your Gmail to Make Filling Out Web Forms Easier

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

Google Chrome is making it easier to autofill online forms with more than just contact information and credit card numbers. For users with Personal Intelligence enabled, Gemini will now suggest items like order numbers, tracking information, membership IDs, and booking confirmations from Gmail messages when completing forms in Chrome.

Chrome's expanded autofill capabilities use Gemini to read your emails and surface suggestions, meaning you don't have to click back and forth between tabs or manually search for codes or confirmations in your inbox. When you click a form field that has a corresponding piece of data, a pop-up menu appears and indicates that an item is "Suggested by Gemini." You can click this to autofill the suggestion as well as open an additional menu to see the specific source (the original email) or remove the suggestion. The latter doesn't delete anything from Gmail; it simply dismisses the suggestion in Chrome.

As Android Police reports, Google started testing enhanced autofill in Chrome this summer using data from other connected apps like Google Photos. The feature currently rolling out is specific to Gmail and is coming first to U.S. users who have Personal Intelligence enabled on desktop as well as in the Android and iOS apps when using Gemini in Chrome.

In the blog post announcing the enhanced autofill feature, Google states that "sensitive data is encrypted" and that users can manage autofill, including enabling or disabling enhanced suggestions, via Chrome's settings.
